deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 31% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 26% last year; 26%/yr over 3 years — roughly in line with its recent growth.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: -5% — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $-5 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 2% (3 years ago -1%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $11.7B, up 48% from a year ago — about 2.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $5.1B, up 26% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Earnings-quality red flags
flags: Stock-based pay is 23% of sales — a real cost to shareholders that cash-flow figures leave out.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 26%/yr over 3 years and 35%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today -1% vs a 5-year range of -10–1% (median -6%): in the middle of its range.
deeper.margin_position: in the middle of its range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: No buybacks or dividends reported over the last 12 months. Share count up 4.7% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $1.65, down 0% in 90 days (up 3% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $1.28, down 2% in 90 days (up 2% in the last 30); 2 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By product, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Subscription 95% of sales, up 29%; Professional services 5% of sales, up 23%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.sub: latest quarter +28% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $5.7B

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Operating margin -1%: it spends more to run the business than it earns from sales.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 1860% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 2232× last year's profit (higher than 81% of the last 5 years); only 127× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.
